articles.title: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver 'optimistic' of challenging top four in Dutch GP after Qualifying improvement
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton heads all-Ferrari third row with McLaren and Mercedes cars ahead on grid, but Briton believes Scuderia can still have a say over the race distance; watch the Dutch Grand Prix on Sunday at 2pm (build-up from 12.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
​​​​​​Ferrari are Mercedes' nearest challengers in both world championship races but qualified three tenths of a second away from pole at Zandvoort, F1's first event back after its summer break.

Fifth-fastest Hamilton and sixth-fastest Charles Leclerc will start behind both Mercedes and McLaren cars for a race that Lando Norris starts on pole position.

But fifth on the grid represented a step forward for Hamilton compared to the earlier Sprint sessions when he had qualified and finished seventh.

"Much different session, much different car," said Hamilton, who pipped Leclerc to the head of the third row with his final lap of Q3, to Sky Sports F1 after main qualifying.

"In Practice, the car felt great and was consistent but there are always areas you feel you can improve so we made subtle changes to try and fix those improvements and it flipped the car on its head and it was horrible through Sprint Qualifying and the Sprint. I had no confidence in the balance.

"We made all these changes into Qualifying so I was learning a new car again, a new balance which I'm much happier with - trying to progress with it and learning with only like six laps was a challenge.

"Also all the Mercedes [powered cars] are ahead and we know we have a bit of a deficit on power so I think our race pace should be better and the car is better for the race."

Saturday's earlier Sprint race had appeared to prove that Ferrari's car was a competitive proposition around the twisty, undulating Zandvoort circuit.

Leclerc finished second, 1.3s behind winner George Russell, with his overtake on Norris with six laps to go the only change of position in the top 10 after the opening lap.

And despite the track not being especially friendly for overtaking, Hamilton is not ruling out the prospect of the SF-26 getting in the mix at the front again.

"Fifth is not the greatest but it could be far worse, so I'm grateful to be there but of course I wish I was up further ahead.

"However, our race pace was good in the Sprint. Charles had good race pace and the car is in a better place

"Hopefully with the right strategy and right execution I think hopefully we can challenge the cars ahead."

What went wrong for Leclerc after Sprint promise?

Leclerc's overtake on Norris for second place with six laps to go in the Sprint had proved a relative surprise given he had been the only one of the front runners to run the 24-lap race on the soft tyres, a compound which is initially the fastest but on which performance falls away more quickly.

He had therefore been tipped to contend for pole but the Monegasque never ultimately appeared a contender in any of the three knockout sections.

"I don't think the conditions played a role," said Leclerc. "I think we changed the power strategies a bit too much throughout qualifying then in Q3 I had some weird things going on, so we lost a bit of performance there.

"At no time during qualifying [did I have] the potential of pole."

Dropped to sixth on Sunday's grid thanks to Hamilton's late improvement, Leclerc added on his race prospects: "Realistically it will be very difficult to overtake on track but we will do our best and see where we end up.

"Starting from sixth doesn't make our life easy, so it will be a tough race but the pace is there so I hope we can do something with strategy and offset ourselves to the others."

Team principal Frederic Vasseur, though, took heart from their Sprint performance and said the fact the race was likely to be a multi-stop affair could play in their favour.

"The race pace in the Sprint was very strong so we will try to come back," said the Frenchman.

"We had a good comparison between the two [tyre] compounds [in the Sprint] which is probably the best preparation we can have for the race.

"It's very difficult to overtake. It will probably be two or three pit stops which mean everything is open."

He also said the latest round of SF-26 upgrades, which include a new floor which was thought to be added to the car after the weekend's sole practice session on Friday, were performing as expected.

"It's working as per the plan," added Vasseur. "From the beginning of the season, every time we brought something it's worked per the plan.

"It's a positive side of the development this year. We are bringing a lot of upgrades at each race, not big ones, so we are not expecting to [gain] five tenths per race. But it's working as expected."

articles.title: Lando Norris: McLaren driver says he 'still believes' title fightback is possible after claiming Dutch GP pole
articles.summary: Lando Norris beat Mercedes duo George Russell and Kimi Antonelli to pole in Zandvoort; reigning world champion Norris claimed McLaren's first win of the season in the previous round; watch the Dutch Grand Prix on Sunday at 2pm (build-up from 12.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
​​​​​​The McLaren driver produced a dominant race victory in the final race before the sport's summer break in Hungary and made it two successive pole positions by topping qualifying in Zandvoort on Saturday.

Norris' pole came after he had reduced his deficit to championship leader Kimi Antonelli to 90 points by finishing ahead of the Mercedes driver in the Sprint earlier on Saturday.

In qualifying, Norris edged out the other Mercedes of George Russell for pole, with Antonelli having to settle for third behind his team-mate.

Norris said: "There's no point in thinking about it. Just focus on tomorrow. I honestly don't care what I'm doing next weekend or the weekend after.

"It's nice to know there's a possibility."

Antonelli leads Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton at the top of the standings by 53 points, with Saturday's Sprint winner Russell a further three points back. Norris, who's fifth in the standings, also trails Ferrari's Charles Leclerc by 11 points.

Norris appeared to be in a head-to-head battle with his McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri for last year's title before Red Bull's Max Verstappen surged back into contention and eventually finished just two points behind the champion.

Verstappen's cause was aided by both McLarens being disqualified from the Las Vegas Grand Prix and a strategic error from the eventual constructors' champions at the Qatar Grand Prix, which Norris referenced as he plotted his own 2026 comeback.

"Of course, I'm hoping both Mercedes get a double DSQ in Vegas like we did and decide not to box in Qatar for a free pit stop," Norris said.

"So, as long as they make the same mistakes, it'll probably be just as easy, but every year is different.

"For me, we're still trying to play catch up with certain things, but I'm getting everything out of it for now and that's all I can be pleased about.

"I'm happy. It's still a very long way to go. I'm optimistic. I still believe that it's possible and that's all I need for now."

Russell, who must leapfrog Norris on Sunday to complete a Sprint-Grand Prix double in Zandvoort, believes he is benefiting from his position in the championship having removed pressure.

The 28-year-old started the season as the clear title favourite but has been surprisingly outperformed by Antonelli, who doesn't turn 20 until two days after Sunday's race.

Russell said: "After the break, I just feel way more relaxed. I don't feel I've got anything to lose. The pressure's off. I'm just going to go out, enjoy it.

"I don't even really feel in a fight. It's not mine to lose, it's mine to gain. That's the mentality I've got, and I feel it's going to help me. I'm just enjoying driving."

Despite his change in mindset, Russell shared his belief that the title race could swing very quickly over the 11 remaining rounds that follow Sunday's race.

"There's more points on offer from this point until the end of the season than we've had so far," Russell said.

"It changes so, so quick. We already saw it earlier in the season - at one point I was almost 70 points down, got within 25, went up to 60. It's ebbs and flows and it's far from over. Long way to go.

"I think the Ferraris are looking great. Lando's been on pole for the last two races as well, so you can't count anybody out.

"We've got these upgrades coming. We've got to hope that they work. It only takes one issue with an upgrade and it doesn't work as you expect, and before you know it, you're not fighting at the front week in, week out, and they can be big points missed."

Antonelli: Weekend has been a wake-up call

While Antonelli could quite easily end the weekend with a bigger title lead than he begun it with, the Italian is already describing it as a "wake-up call" for him.

Antonelli made an error in the first part of Sprint Qualifying on Friday that damaged his car and left him compromised for the rest of the session, which contributed to him only managing to take fifth on the grid, before he finished the 24-lap race in fourth.

The 19-year-old, who is driving just his second season in F1, was also frustrated with himself for making an error in on his final run in Saturday's full-length qualifying session.

Antonelli said: "I don't feel any extra pressure, but it was a very good wake-up call this weekend, that you can never lower your guard.

"Because when you do that, I did a mistake yesterday and today I did a mistake in Q3.

"It's not that I'm driving more tense or anything, but it's just I feel this weekend is a good wake-up call and to just, again, put things in the right place at the right time and just deliver the result when it counts."

articles.title: NASCAR Legend Jeff Gordon Wins IROC Street Race in Washington, D.C. at 55 Years Old
articles.summary: NASCAR Hall of Famer Jeff Gordon has won an individual race for the first time in 11 years.
articles.body:
NASCAR Hall of Famer Jeff Gordon has won an individual race for the first time in 11 years.

Gordon claimed two first-place finishes Saturday as the International Race of Champions returned to Washington, D.C. ahead of the Freedom 250 Grand Prix.

The 55-year-old drove both 10-lap races around the National Mall in a No. 24 car owned by Rick Hendrick.

York Responded to Ad on Prostitution Site Before Arrest

Gordon's last individual first-place victory took place in 2015 with a Cup Series win at Martinsville Speedway. He retired from full-time racing following the 2015 season.

He returned to the top of the podium Saturday after passing Helio Castroneves to take the lead in the first race.

He overtook Castroneves and Tony Kanaan in the second race to sweep the day. Fellow NASCAR Hall of Famer Kurt Busch finished the competition in second place.

This marked the first street race for Gordon, who retired as NASCAR's all-time leader in road course wins.

The IROC event preceded the IndyCar Freedom 250, which is set to take place on the National Mall later Saturday afternoon.

articles.title: El otro juez del Mundial de Fórmula 1
articles.standfirst: El británico 'alucinó' después de firmar el mejor crono en Zandvoort y demuestra que McLaren sigue al alza tras su paquete de mejoras
articles.summary: El británico 'alucinó' después de firmar el mejor crono en Zandvoort y demuestra que McLaren sigue al alza tras su paquete de mejoras
articles.body: No había un hombre más feliz en Zandvoort, con ese clima tan típico del norte de España, que Lando Norris. El mismo piloto que hace un año en el mismo trazado se rompía en la radio. Pero el británico ya es campeón y demuestra que es un animador en la batalla, aunque el Mundial marcha demasiado lejos para sus intereses (tiene 134 puntos por los 224 del líder Antonelli). Buscará su segundo triunfo (15:00 horas, DAZN) consecutivo desde la pole en el Gran Premio de los Países Bajos y puede meterse en los asuntos de los candidatos. De hecho, el sábado de Holanda fue un mensaje claro del nuevo Lando. Sufrió por la mañana en el sprint (tercero) y se repuso. "No tenemos más ritmos, no pasa nada", decía por la mañana. Y la pole cambió su semblante y discurso. "Es la mejor vuelta de mi vida", lanzaba tras su 18ª pole de su carrera. Lo que no se interpretaba era su ironía. "No lo fue, no. No fue mi actuación más limpia, pero pude arriesgarme en las frenadas e ir mejor en las zonas de alta velocidad", expresó. Pero ni su ironía cambia la cosa. Norris puede molestar a los Mercedes, quitarles puntos y seguir su particular presión. "Esta pole nos confirma la tendencia que vemos. El coche funciona muy bien en la alta carga y sabemos que trabaja bien con la nueva goma blanda que nos da mucha adherencia", analizaba su jefe, Andrea Stella. Las mejoras de McLaren se hacen notar y tienen ventaja ante Mercedes o Ferrari. Eso sí, también hay un reto: la degradación. "Nos lo enseñó la sprint, tenemos que mejorar con neumáticos usados y reducir la degradación para tratar de ser competitivos en carrera", añadió Stella. Allí mejoran sus competidores y el tablero puede agitarse aunque Zandvoort no permite muchos movimientos en una pista fundamentalmente de posición con puntos contados de pasar si hay ventajas. Y el Mundial abrirse a más escenarios. Con Russell al lado de Norris y pudiendo atacar. "Voy carrera a carrera, no puedo decir que todos mis problemas se han acabado", reconocía. Y Antonelli defendiendo. "No estoy muy contento porque sufro en confianza y ritmo. No tenía una buena sensación del coche. Lo más importante es que estamos terceros y sabemos qué jugar en la carrera", cerró. Atacarán a Lando y el enésimo juicio al Mundial se abrirá en Holanda. Hagan sus apuestas.

articles.title: ¡El enésimo lío de Verstappen y Russell!: "Ahora llorará por la radio..."
articles.standfirst: El neerlandés rozó un pequeño drama con el británico y es otro capítulo más de su peculiar relación en la Fórmula 1
articles.summary: El neerlandés rozó un pequeño drama con el británico y es otro capítulo más de su peculiar relación en la Fórmula 1
articles.body: Destinados a encontrarse. Hay parejas, exparejas, amantes y determinado tipo de personas que acaban confluyendo una y otra vez. Y como la Fórmula 1 es otra representación más de la vida, en el Gran Premio de los Países Bajos unieron sus destinos dos estrellas que siempre tienen su tira y afloja, George Russell y Max Verstappen. Cómo no. Dos viejos conocidos. En la clasificación, su episodio llegó en la Q3. En una de las primeras salidas a pista, Red Bull sacó a Verstappen del box justo al mismo tiempo que Mercedes hacía lo propio con Russell. Rozaron el toque y el neerlandés reaccionó a través de su radio. "Ahora George [Russell] llorará por la radio contando que fue una salida insegura. No hubo nada", lanzó. Con cierta gracia, como siempre que se cruza con el británico. Acabó en nada y ninguna sanción o castigo cayó a los pilotos. Pero revivió esa rivalidad que tuvo su último capítulo en Austria tras aquella pole de Russell con banderas amarillas. Max ironizó por la radio tras el episodio. "¿Banderas amarillas? Supongo que tendré que acelerar", soltó recordando otros episodios de sus batallas con momentos más conflictivos como el 2024 en el que se prometieron casi chocar. Además, da la casualidad que los dos pilotos unen sus caminos en el fin de semana que se confirmó que su futuro no dependerá del otro. Verstappen, millonada mediante, fue renovado por Red Bull y Russell seguirá en Mercedes. "No temía por mi lugar, son cosas de la prensa", lanzó el británico.  Volviendo a la actualidad, en carrera (15:00 horas, DAZN) saldrá Russell desde la primera línea -con Norris en pole- y Verstappen será séptimo tras un fin de semana sin ritmo y donde no presenta la mejor de sus caras.

articles.title: Newey le da la razón a Alonso para el próximo salto del AMR26
articles.standfirst: La manejabilidad es el aspecto clave sobre el que quiere sustentarse el futuro cercano del equipo de Silverstone
articles.summary: La manejabilidad es el aspecto clave sobre el que quiere sustentarse el futuro cercano del equipo de Silverstone
articles.body: Carlos Sainz, siempre analítico y capaz de detectar las principales líneas que se desarrollan en la Fórmula 1, era muy directo cuando la prensa española le preguntaba tras la clasificación del Gran Premio de los Países Bajos. “Los Aston van tan rápido en curvas y carrera que no sé cómo estamos por delante”, reconocía. En la qualy, el 55 batió con un coche inferior a los AMR26 que pasaron de la esperanza de Hungría a las primeras dudas. No son del paso adelante, pues existe. Pero sí de un paquete que está lejos de ser optimizado y necesita un salto de calidad desde la fábrica. “En pista ya no podemos hacer mucho más”, apuntaba Fernando Alonso. Lo vinculaba a la manejabilidad que permite la unidad de potencia, uno de esos términos de moda en la Fórmula 1. Con los nuevos motores y el cambio del frenado y el uso del freno motor, ahora gana importancia para dar confianza a los pilotos y permitirles desde la recarga de energía hasta seguir atacando. Y Honda no ha dado con la clave en todo el año. El propulsor nipón es mejor -para empezar, el paddock estima que hay unos 10 o 15 caballos de mejora en Holanda-, pero necesita una labor que los pilotos piden y Adrian Newey, el gran padre técnico del proyecto, da como clave. “Lo que hemos aprendido es que necesitamos mejorar esa manejabilidad y al obtenerlo encontraremos más rendimiento”, explicaba el británico. Newey seguirá liderando el proyecto desde el punto de vista de los ajustes aerodinámicos y una rebaja de peso que debería aparecer entre Monza y Azerbaiyán, con Honda en el debe de la otra parte. “Los pilotos reportan avances en el chasis y la aerodinámica, sabemos que hay mucho mejor ritmo pero debemos desbloquear más potencial todavía”, reconocía el británico. No es la primera vez en la que pide más a la parte japonesa del proyecto, aunque nada se compara a aquel inicio de Australia en el que todos los problemas salieron a la luz. Ahora el coche es mejor. “La mejora es increíble”, desvelaba Alonso. Pero dentro de ese salto, todavía hay una parte que el equipo puede permitirse conseguir para seguir compitiendo. En la zona media, el coche puede estar a la zaga de Alpine, Racing Bulls o Audi, pero desde el seno británico se pide más. “No lideraremos esa zona media, pero no estaremos lejos”, apuntó Mike Krack, otro de sus máximos representantes, en el inicio del fin de semana.

articles.title: Adiós a Zandvoort: la F1 se despide de un GP que quiso mantener
articles.standfirst: La carrera del Gran Premio de los Países Bajos marca el final de una era de una de las citas más bonitas del calendario
articles.summary: La carrera del Gran Premio de los Países Bajos marca el final de una era de una de las citas más bonitas del calendario
articles.body: Llegar a la pequeña y coqueta Zandvoort desde Ámsterdam o alguna localidad cercana de los Países Bajos es relativamente sencillo, tanto en un vehículo particular, que navega en el mar de bicicletas holandesas camino del trabajo o del colegio, como en los trenes del país. Pero en los últimos días del verano se vuelve en un casi imposible. Porque la marea naranja traga a todo y todos, grita a su héroe Max Verstappen y aterriza en el bautizado como Gran Premio de la felicidad. Uno que se despide del calendario de la Fórmula 1 con la carrera de 2026. Y el que, curiosamente, nadie quiso que corriese ese final. La Fórmula 1 actual vive permanentemente en alerta para encontrar más aficionados, mercados y lugares. Y Zandvoort, cada vez más moderno, cumple al llenar sus gradas y no fallar a la cita. Más Verstappen, al que todos quieren tener muy presente. Tras volver en 2021 (no estuvo entre 1986 y 2020) al calendario comenzó el éxito, pero a la hora de renovar su última vinculación llegó el imposible. La organización explicó que era una empresa privada y no podían exponer sus beneficios con una renovación (con coste dependiendo del estatus) o entrada en la rotación. Mientras tanto, la F1 ofreció opciones (según su CEO, Stefano Domenicali) que no se terminaron de confirmar. Zandvoort se cayó. El calendario pierde a los Países Bajos, aunque el efecto Verstappen sigue siendo notable en circuitos como Austria o Hungría, y la parroquia oranje no falla. Pero sin su santuario. Desapareciendo de un calendario que ahora tendrá una nueva cara en el regreso a Portimao o Turquía del curso que viene, y el estreno en tres semanas de un Madring donde ya se respiran carreras al empezar el test de F3. Contratos en mano, la F1 abrirá una etapa en la que destaca la rotación de Spa y Montmeló, y las próximas renovaciones llegarán con los circuitos que finalizan su vinculación en 2028. Ocurre con Singapur, la Ciudad de México o la novedad de Portimao. En el otro lado de la balanza, Madrid, Canadá, Mónaco (2035), Bahréin (2036), Australia, Las Vegas (2037), Miami y Austria (2041) tienen el larguísimo plazo en la categoría reina asegurado. Zandvoort se quedará, de momento, como una etapa de felicidad en las gradas, lleno absoluto y la presentación en sociedad de un panorama diferente en las carreras al mezclar la emoción de la velocidad con la fiesta que representa la música desde bien entrada la mañana de cada día de Gran Premio.

articles.title: ¡Gran accidente de Verstappen en la primera vuelta!
articles.standfirst: El neerlandés vivió un difícil fin de semana en casa justo después de anunciar una renovación histórica
articles.summary: El neerlandés vivió un difícil fin de semana en casa justo después de anunciar una renovación histórica
articles.body: Max Verstappen ha vivido en su casa, el Gran Premio de los Países Bajos, dos caras completamente opuestas para cualquier deportista. La de una renovación histórica, que le catapulta al podio universal de los que más ganan y compite con nombres legendarios como Leo Messi o Karim Benzema. Y también una cita torcida que se cerró de la peor forma, con uno de sus peores accidentes sin haber cruzado la primera vuelta de carrera.  Además, todo el contexto es triste para Max. Es la última carrera de Zandvoort en la Fórmula 1, la grada vive por su figura y no pudo celebrarlo. Todo lo contrario. La salida en condiciones mixtas complicó el inicio para los candidatos y Verstappen vivió muchos problemas y un final en el muro con un golpe que le provoca otro cero en un campeonato que ve a más de 100 puntos y sin opciones de una remontada similar a la de 2025. El accidentado inicio de carrera para Verstappen empezó pronto. En la salida se encontró con la patinada de George Russell que provocó un atasco para pasar en la primera curva. Tuvo que reaccionar y tomar un exterior de emergencia y allí se emparejó con Liam Lawson, su compañero excepcional tras la lesión de Hadjar. Los Red Bull vivieron sus más y sus menos, pero Max pudo tirar.  Hasta la última curva. Todavía estaba mojada y Verstappen se pegó al interior a toda velocidad. No pudo controlar al coche y terminó escupiéndole hacia el muro. El destrozo del Red Bull fue completo, con sus piezas saltando por los aires en Zandvoort. "¿Está bien? Lo he visto y es grande", preguntaba el propio Lawson. Por suerte, se quedará en el sustazo, como el que Bortoleto vivió unos puestos por detrás. En su caso, sin consecuencia alguna. En el curso 2026, el golpe de Holanda se convierte en el cuarto abandono del cuatro veces campeón este curso. Con problemas mecánicos en China y Mónaco, el golpe de Gran Bretaña y un accidente que entristecerá a los miles de aficionados que visten la camiseta naranja en su honor. No está siendo su año, ni con 450 millones preparados para entrar en sus arcas al renovar con Red Bull.

articles.title: Norris impide el fiestón de Antonelli y Alonso se exhibe
articles.standfirst: El asturiano termina noveno en el Gran Premio de los Países Bajos tras un larguísimo 'stint' inicial y Sainz vuelve a sufrir (16º)
articles.summary: El asturiano termina noveno en el Gran Premio de los Países Bajos tras un larguísimo 'stint' inicial y Sainz vuelve a sufrir (16º)
articles.body: Al campeón del mundo de Fórmula 1 se le debe un respeto. No, no es el piloto más brillante de todos los que forman la parrilla. Y tampoco parece que podrá defender su corona en 2026. Pero Lando Norris sí que es un talento especial y firmó una de sus mejores victorias en Zandvoort, una que sabe a algo muy grande. Porque todo hacía indicar que Kimi Antonelli iba a llevarse el enésimo mar de merecidos elogios, pero la dupla Lando-McLaren cortó una fiesta segura en el Gran Premio de los Países Bajos. Es el picante del campeonato, la F1 lo necesita. "Voy carrera a carrera", relataba. El Mundial, eso sí, huele a Antonelli. El de Bolonia evitó mayores problemas y el segundo final es otro golpe a la competencia ya que amplía su margen a 59 puntos con George Russell, 3º final, y Lewis Hamilton. De hecho, sus dos alternativas pelearon por el podio en una batalla que tuvo altas dosis de drama a través de la radio. Y nadie puede salir de Zandvoort sin valorar muy positivamente el recital de Fernando Alonso. Sumó dos puntos más tras un 9º de oro gracias a una degradación increíble con el blando y poder mantener con ritmo a coches más rápidos en la parte final. Por fin recibe la estrategia buena y el piloto puede hacer el resto. El picante en Zandvoort lo puso, para empezar, la salida. Y tiene connotaciones mundialistas. El suelo estaba ligeramente húmedo tras el tradicional y diario chaparrón holandés, y George Russell siguió como el pupas de la categoría. Patinó, no atacó al poleman Norris y Antonelli pasó. Aunque peor suerte todavía vivió Max Verstappen. El héroe local se despidió de su pista con un golpe descomunal -bandera roja- en ese primer giro tras tocar el interior mojado del último peralte. Este 2026 no está siendo su año, ni con 450 millones de euros dispuestos a entrar a sus arcas tras la renovación.  No serán 450 millones -de momento-, pero Kimi Antonelli también vale oro. Tras el KO de Verstappen, al italiano le tocó poner a Zandvoort en pie y fue en la resalida de la bandera roja. Tomó el interior ante Norris, alargó la frenada de la 1 y pasó. En su punto débil del 2026 había encontrado un argumento de poder, aunque no tuvo continuidad en términos de ritmo cuando la degradación apareció. En la segunda parte de carrera, Antonelli y Norris batallaron en la distancia de adelantamiento y con los duros llegó el desenlace. Al de Mercedes le sentó como un tiro en su tren trasero y el ritmo cayó por completo. Eso lo aprovechó la tracción y carga del Mclaren para un recital final de Lando. Norris ya no es un blando, ni nada parecido. Ahora es un campeón y corre como tal, pues sin nada que perder se lanzó a por Antonelli en la curva 1 cuando los dos perseguían a un Hamilton sin parada. El campeón defensor alargó el exterior, rebasó a Kimi y después hizo lo propio con el de Ferrari. El golpe al Gran Premio, su segunda victoria consecutiva del 2026. "No tenía muchas más oportunidades, sabía que era en ese momento y la frenada me dio la carrera", admitió el de McLaren. Cortó el show de Antonelli, que cruzó segundo y más líder la meta. Aunque no estuvo libre de líos, pues su victoria desapareció en la mitad final de carrera y tuvo sus más y sus menos con Russell. El otro piloto de Mercedes no hizo una parada extra y tenía una ligera ventaja que desde la radio le hicieron perder. Sirvió para terminar de cerrar el podio de Antonelli y Russell pudo mantener el suyo tras un gran tirón final que neutralizó a los Ferrari competitivos con el desgaste. El desgaste también fue lo que colocó a Fernando Alonso en su mejor lugar del 2026, 9º. El único que pudo acabar a una parada, pues el AMR26 ha construido una base que dará rédito, tarde o temprano. La degradación es mucho menor a la del resto y alargó un neumático blando hasta el giro 34. Más que nadie. Eso le reportó poder pasar a Ocon, uno de sus rivales tras una primera parte de carrera en la que también sumó una buena salida con un exterior increíble sobre su compañero Stroll. Y esa estrategia siguió permitiendo el tirón. Batalló con éxito ante Albon y alargó sus duros mientras venían por detrás rivales con coches mucho mejores de la zona media. Que no tenían ese punto más en gestión del asturiano ya que Alonso cerró puertas, Gasly atacó en la lejanía y Tsunoda ni se acercó. 9º que sabe a mucho más. Aston va llegando. Carlos Sainz también optó por la vía del milagro con un neumático y su parada sólo tuvo un ejemplo más tardío en la de Alonso. Fue su método de supervivencia tras ralentizar a los más rápidos de la zona media y esperar a algún cambio que no llegó. De hecho, le metió en batallas que no dieron resultado alguno. Primero le tocó con Lindblad y después con un Albon menos cuidadoso con los neumáticos. Los dos compañeros entraron en pelea y en la 1 llegó un toque que terminó con sanción con el español. La trayectoria no fue la mejor y el plano en su neumático hizo el resto hasta terminar contactando. De nuevo, no se dio. Y el Williams sigue sin levantar cabeza ni en carreras con escenarios diferentes.

articles.title: Deauville: Aventure ends Diamond Necklace's unbeaten record with Sumbe Prix Jean et Louis Romanet win
articles.summary: Aventure produced an upset in the Sumbe Prix Jean et Louis Romanet, defeating the previously-unbeaten Diamond Necklace in the Deauville Group One; also on the card, Senorita Bonita dazzled for the Simon and Ed Crisford team in the Prix Morny
articles.body:
Aidan O'Brien's daughter of St Mark's Basilica was expected to dazzle once again in France, as she had done when landing the Prix Marcel Boussac, Poule d'Essai Des Pouliches and Prix de Diane on her travels during what was an unbeaten six-race career to date.

However, she had no answer to the experience of her Christophe Ferland-trained elder, who added to last year's Group One strike in the Prix Vermeille.

In a close-up third was the Charlie Johnston-trained Timeforshowcasing, who ran a big race in the hands of Jack Mitchell.

Pierre-Yves Bureau, racing manager for owners the Wertheimer brothers, said: "We're very happy and when she won the Prix Corrida earlier this year we were very happy but then made a mistake by running over a mile and a half in the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud.

"There was a strong field of fillies including Diamond Necklace, but what our mare did is just wonderful, she is such a champion. We will be very happy to have her as a broodmare one day, but we will enjoy her racing for the moment!"

Second to Bluestocking in the 2024 Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe, Aventure earned a quote of 20/1 for this year's renewal by Paddy Power following her triumph over O'Brien's star performer in the hands of Maxime Guyon.

However, there will be no third attempt at Europe's richest middle-distance prize for the five-year-old who will instead remain at 10 furlongs for the Prix de l'Opera post the main event on Arc day before a possible trip to Keeneland.

Bureau added: "It's quite unusual, but this filly is getting more speed with age and 10 furlongs is her perfect trip now. She has been really well prepared for this race.

"The plan is to run her in the Prix de l'Opera and then if everything goes well we might take her to the Breeders' Cup for the Filly & Mare Turf, but we will take it step-by-step and one race at a time. The next step will be the Prix de l'Opera."

Senorita Bonita proves jet-propelled in Prix Morny

Senorita Bonita demonstrated her devastating turn of foot to scorch to Sumbe Prix Morny glory.

The 900,000 guineas top lot from April's Craven Breeze-Up sale, Simon and Ed Crisford's filly arrived on the Normandy coast looking to follow up her victory in Newmarket's Duchess of Cambridge Stakes, a win that received a timely boost by Lowther Stakes scorer Libertango earlier this week.

Held up towards the rear by Oisin Murphy, with Clive Cox's Royal Ascot winner Orthodox ahead, the daughter of Starspangledbanner had plenty of ground to make up on Aidan O'Brien's front-running Carry The Flag entering the final third of the contest.

However, once the champion jockey stepped on the accelerator the response was instant, as not only did Senorita Bonita rapidly eat away at the deficit but then surged readily clear of the long-time pace-setter for a thoroughly impressive victory.

Simon Crisford said: "She's shown a great turn of front and obviously they set some very good fractions up front but she finished off super well - she galloped out strongly.

"She was a little bit slow out of the gates and behind the bridle early, but they were going quick and the race set up for the closers and she was the best of the closers.

"At halfway I briefly thought we might have a mountain to climb here, but she's got such a good turn of foot that at the furlong pole you could see she was going to come home strong."

It was the father and son training team's second victory in the Group One race after Vandeek in 2023, while it continues the fine record of fillies in the contest following on from Venetian Sun's triumph for Karl Burke 12 months ago.

The Victorious Racing-owned Senorita Bonita will now go in search of further top honours in Newmarket's Cheveley Park Stakes and was made 5/2 by bookmakers for a race where she could meet former foe Libertango once again, as well as another recent York winner, Sun Goddess.

"All roads lead to the Cheveley Park now at the end of September and that was a fantastic performance," continued Crisford.

"It was a deep, deep renewal and it was a really, really pleasing effort and she's looked really impressive there.

"Any Group One is fantastic to win and we are all just delighted. It's a great testament to the staff back at home and everyone involved and it's great to win for Shaikh Nasser (bin Hamed Al Khalifa) and Shaikh Khalid (bin Hamed Al Khalifa)."

articles.title: Sainz: "Me encontré un bache gigante y me llevé a Alex, una faena"
articles.standfirst: Carlos acabó con un accidente en Holanda, aunque pudo terminar la carrera
articles.summary: Carlos acabó con un accidente en Holanda, aunque pudo terminar la carrera
articles.body: Carlos Sainz acabó 16º en el GP de Países Bajos, con dos vueltas perdidas y tras un desafortunado accidente con su compañero Alex Albon. El ritmo fue mejor de lo que se esperaba en carrera y llegó a estar por momentos cerca de los puntos, pero tras la parada inicial, todo fue a peor. "Sí, un fin de semana en general yo creo muy complicado, donde nos ha faltado ritmo todo el fin de semana y luego encima al final, con unas gomas que ya estaba en las últimas, intentando defenderme de Alex en la curva 1, y me ha pillado por sorpresa un bache gigante que hay en la frenada, que además cuanto más por dentro vas y más por dentro frenas más te pega el coche abajo y bloqueas de delante. Luego me lo llevo puesto, así que una pena porque realmente  luchando por la posición que estamos luchando lo último que quieres es acabar con un contacto con tu compañero de equipo", resumía Sainz sobre lo sucedido. "Es una faena, pero demuestra lo mucho que estamos sufriendo este fin de semana como equipo y la posición en la que estamos que es una posición muy mala. Estos fines de semana donde parece que está todo en contra, todo sale mal", añadía.  Sainz confesaba que era difícil sacar algo positivo: "A nivel personal no, no hay mucho positivo este fin de semana... A nivel equipo yo creo que las pruebas que hicimos en cuanto a la consistencia de las piezas que ponemos en el coche, yo creo que vamos a extraer cosas interesantes de cara al futuro y espero que nos ayuden, nos enseñen un poco una luz en cuanto al desarrollo", deseaba. "Hemos tenido muchos problemas últimamente. Ahora se trata de apretar los dientes más que nunca, antes de la llegada de esas evoluciones de Bakú, aunque no sea una gran mejora, pero... Nada más que apretar los dientes yo creo que tenemos que utilizar es estas dos últimas carreras antes del 'upgrade' para probar cosas igual un poco fuera de nuestra zona de confort como equipo, encontrar cosas o probar cosas que igual no nos interesan entender y luego cuando llegue el momento de la mejora, pues ojalá podamos estar un poco más cerca y podamos divertirnos un poco más luchando con los de adelante", explicaba sobre los próximos pasos del equipo. En cuanto a la estrategia y apurar con los blandos iniciales, Carlos no se lamentaba. "No había estrategia hoy que hacer porque no íbamos rápido... cuando no vas rápido no hay estrategia buena", cerraba.

articles.title: Dutch GP: Lando Norris beats Kimi Antonelli to victory in Zandvoort to claim second successive race win
articles.summary: Lando Norris wins Dutch Grand Prix to secure back-to-back victories; Kimi Antonelli extends overall championship lead to 59 points by finishing second; Norris reduces title-race deficit to 83 points; George Russell holds off Lewis Hamilton for third; Max Verstappen crashed out on first lap
articles.body:
McLaren's Norris started on pole in Zandvoort but lost the lead to Antonelli at an early standing restart after Red Bull's Max Verstappen triggered a red flag at his home race by crashing out at the end of the first lap.

After struggling to pressure Antonelli on the first stint, Norris was far quicker after switching onto a hard tyre at the first round of pit stops, and eventually passed the Mercedes after emerging from his second stop with much fresher tyres than the Italian.

Mercedes left George Russell vulnerable to missing out on a podium by ordering him to let Antonelli through to second in the closing stages, but the Brit was ultimately just able to hold off Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton for third.

Antonelli's championship lead grows to 59 points with Russell taking over second from Hamilton in the standings despite the pair having the same points total, while reigning champion Norris reduces his deficit to the leader to 83 points.

Reigning constructors' champions McLaren failed to claim a win in the opening 10 grands prix of the season, but a significant upgrade brought to the final round before the summer break in Hungary propelled Norris to a dominant success in Budapest.

Had it not been for Norris giving up the lead with a poor getaway at the early restart, this victory could have been similarly dominant, leaving little doubt that the Brit appears the driver most likely to challenge Antonelli for the title over the remaining 11 rounds despite his current position of fourth in the standings.

Celebrating his victory over team radio moments after taking the chequered flag, Norris declared: "Let's keep bringing upgrades. Let's keep bringing performance. The fight is still on. Let's keep going."

Charles Leclerc was fifth for Ferrari, whose pitwall endured a nervy final lap as their cars almost collided when the Monegasque closed up on the battle between Hamilton and Russell.

Oscar Piastri, who remains unable to come anywhere close to matching the pace of his team-mate Norris, was sixth.

Liam Lawson, deputising as Verstappen's Red Bull team-mate in place of the injured Isack Hadjar, completed a solid weekend by taking seventh.

Nico Hulkenberg, who did brilliantly to avoid a shunt with his Audi team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto on the first lap when the Brazilian spun just metres behind the Verstappen crash, made the most of the escape to take eighth.

Fernando Alonso exhibited Aston Martin's improvement following upgrades to both their chassis and Honda power unit by managing his tyres brilliantly on a one-stop strategy to claim ninth, while Pierre Gasly took the final point for Alpine.

Mercedes extended their Constructors' Championship lead over Ferrari to 87 points, while McLaren remained 163 points back from the leaders in third.

Having finished third as Russell took victory in Saturday's Sprint, Norris benefitted from set-up changes made to his car going into full qualifying to beat both Mercedes to pole, but it remained to be seen how the set-up would work over full race distance.

Norris got off the line well to hold the lead at a start made tricky by damp conditions caused by earlier rain, but was forced to do it all over again by the red flag.

Antonelli, who had passed Russell at the first start, pulled off the trick again as he got up the inside of Norris at the first corner and held his nerve to take the lead.

Norris initially applied some pressure to Antonelli but seemed to have little hope of passing the Mercedes at a circuit where overtaking is generally very tricky.

Both pitted at the end of the 21st circuit of the 72-lap race and switched onto a hard tyre, after which the dynamic swung dramatically with Norris clearly faster.

Mercedes opted to pit the under-pressure Antonelli, with McLaren this time leaving Norris out for seven extra laps, giving him fresh rubber to chase for victory on what it appeared would be the final stint.

Norris emerged from the pits just five seconds down on Antonelli and very quickly closed in on the Mercedes, who had the extra challenge of coming up behind Hamilton, who had yet to make his second stop at the time.

As Antonelli looked to go up the inside of Hamilton at the start of lap 54, Norris darted to the outside and went past the Mercedes that way, before easing past Hamilton to take the race lead later in the lap.

"The move was good! I knew I wasn't going to get many chances," Norris said. "Every lap I spent behind them, my odds were getting lower.

"I saw Lewis defended and I knew that was my moment. I did a couple clicks of brake balance, I knew I was going to commit to the braking and that move won me the race. Just well-played from my part. I knew I had to make it."

There was a further twist to come, though, as Haas' Esteban Ocon stopped on track to trigger a virtual safety car, under which Antonelli would pit, bringing him out in third, 12 seconds behind Norris but with tyres that were nine laps fresher.

However, it swiftly became apparent that even with his newer tyres, Antonelli would not have the pace to threaten Norris, with the bigger issue for the Italian getting past his team-mate Russell for second.

With both Ferraris, who also stopped for fresh tyres under the VSC, just a few seconds behind Antonelli, Mercedes ordered Russell to let his team-mate through to avoid a potential situation where they lost both podium places to Hamilton and Leclerc.

That decision initially appeared to have condemned Russell, on much older tyres having not made a third stop, to losing his third place to Hamilton.

But just when Hamilton seemed certain to get himself on the podium, another VSC was declared to allow marshals to clear debris from the track, which gave Russell some much-needed respite before he held off one final charge from Hamilton.

Up ahead, Norris ultimately took the chequered flag 11 seconds clear of Antonelli, with the Brit showing the sort of form that propelled him to a maiden title last year.

Asked about his hopes of retaining his title, Norris said: "It sounds boring, but one race at a time.

"I know a lot of people say it now but it's the truth of it. There's no point thinking that far ahead. I need to concentrate now on having a nice little break [before Monza].

"Obviously two great weekends but we just need to reset and to learn as much as we can. I think there are still plenty of things we need to do better and can do better if we want to fight for a championship."

Zandvoort farewell dampened by Verstappen crash

A week that started with celebration for Red Bull and Verstappen, after Wednesday's announcement that he had extended his contract with the team until the end of 2030, ended on a sour note.

Sunday's race was the last at Zandvoort.

The home fans' expectations were modest after Verstappen had only qualified seventh, but rain coming down about an hour before the race heightened hope the Dutchman could produce some magic before a six-year stint on the F1 calendar for Zandvoort came to an end.

While the rain stopped about 20 minutes before the start, it actually turned out to be Verstappen's downfall.

Approaching the final corner of the first lap, he got on the accelerator too early and spun at high speed into the barrier, triggering a red flag.

Verstappen told Sky Sports F1 : "It was still quite wet in that corner. As soon as I was going through the corner, I could see a little bit of a dry line coming, and I thought from that point on I could accelerate again, but it suddenly then accelerated a lot.

"It caught me out, simple as that. I tried to correct it but couldn't.

"And then you hit the wall, but it could have been a lot worse because there were a lot of cars behind me as well, but luckily that all went well."

articles.title: El mejor Alonso del 2026: "Es justo lo que necesitábamos, ahora el equipo quiere más"
articles.standfirst: El ovetense lleva al Aston Martin a su mejor resultado del curso y reivindica el trabajo en la fábrica con un chasis muy competente
articles.summary: El ovetense lleva al Aston Martin a su mejor resultado del curso y reivindica el trabajo en la fábrica con un chasis muy competente
articles.body: Fernando Alonso firmó en Zandvoort su mejor carrera del 2026. Un trabajado noveno puesto se unió al 10º de Mónaco como lugares de puntos de la temporada y la segunda mitad del curso en la Fórmula 1 toma otro color. El de un AMR26 que permite lanzarse a estrategias diferentes y no se hunde con un motor Honda que no está a la altura de la aerodinámica ideada por Adrian Newey en la fábrica. El noveno fue un resultado trabajadísimo en el que Alonso se lució con un eterno primer stint en el blando. La degradación provoca que el AMR26 trabaje mejor que el resto y pudo pelear con coches teóricamente muy superiores. "Hay rivales que van mucho más veloces de lo normal", admitía el asturiano sobre Gasly o Albon. Por ello, se alargó su parada y aprovechó la ventaja. "No era el plan porque pensábamos en dos paradas, algo más convencional. Pero necesitamos desviarnos de lo normal, porque si estás en tráfico no utilizamos nuestro potencial. Somos rápidos en curvas y lentos en rectas; y nos quedamos atascados tras coches más lentos. Cuando hay pista libre, lo tratamos de utilizar aunque no sea lo más óptimo", analizaba. Se despejó su camino y pudo frenar en seco la progresión de Pierre Gasly y Yuki Tsunoda. Por el camino existió alguna reclamación con su delta del asturiano, pero no fue a más. Consiguió sumar por ritmo y estrategia. "Sumamos un punto en Mónaco con nueve abandonos y hoy sumamos dos sólo con el abandono de Max [Verstappen]. Creo que ha sido merecido y venimos de Budapest donde pudo ser un poco mejor", explicó. Eso sí, no todas las carreras seguirán la misma tónica." Dependerá de cada carrera y de las rectas. No creo que seamos competitivos en Monza, pero en otros circuitos podremos luchar por puntos", agregó. Obviamente, apunta a un motor sin ese paso adelante. Sí de potencia, pero no en facilidad en la conducción. "Es más difícil, y no es algo de blanco y negro por si tienes más potencia o no. La manejabilidad es un aspecto que varía al cambiar de circuito después de un mes y fue difícil Sufrimos en las bajada de marcha y en el freno-motor en curva a curva", explicaba. Lo que todos admiten, tanto en el seno japonés como Newey y el aspecto que deben mejorar.  Al otro lado de la balanza, un chasis que le hace ser optimista. "Sí. Es otro paso adelante con los componentes nuevos. El paquete de Budapest nos hizo entender la dirección y con los datos pudimos optimizarlo. Extraemos el máximo", apuntó el bicampeón. "Tenemos la dirección clara porque vamos bien en las curvas y no te preocupas en ese sentido", añadió. El resultado es un 9º que abre la puerta a la esperanza. "Es lo que necesitábamos", reconoció. Y motiva al equipo. "Ahora nos queda seguir optimizando y trabajar, es un resultado que motiva y todos en las dos fábricas estarán fichando a las 8 porque quieren más", cerró.

articles.title: Max Verstappen: Red Bull driver says huge Dutch Grand Prix crash 'could have been a lot worse'
articles.summary: Max Verstappen had a massive crash when running in seventh on the opening lap of the Dutch Grand Prix; Verstappen walked away unharmed but feels the shunt could have been "a lot worse" at his home event
articles.body:
Verstappen caught too much of the damp kerb through the normally flat-out banked corner and hit the outside barriers hard before coming to a halt in front of a packed Zandvoort crowd.

The severity of the incident caused a red flag but Verstappen walked away unharmed from what is likely to be the last Dutch Grand Prix of his career - as the event does not have a contract beyond this year.

"It was of course still quite wet in that corner. As soon as I was going through the corner, I could see a little bit of a dry line coming, and I thought from that point on I could accelerate again, but it suddenly then accelerated a lot," Verstappen explained to Sky Sports F1 .

"It caught me out, simple as that. I tried to correct it but couldn't. And then you hit the wall, but it could have been a lot worse because there were a lot of cars behind me as well, but luckily that all went well."

Verstappen: Zandvoort highlighted Red Bull are fourth fastest

It was a dramatic end to a disappointing first race after the summer break for Red Bull, just days after Verstappen signed a new contract to stay with the team until at least the end of 2030.

Verstappen started and finish Saturday's Sprint in sixth and was half a second behind pace-setters Mercedes and McLaren in both qualifying sessions.

Having been able to compete at the front in the four races before the summer break, with three podiums in July, it was a surprise to see Red Bull take a step back.

"If you look on average the whole season we have been fourth fastest, I think this weekend really highlighted that," said Verstappen.

"We're a little bit behind, we want to be closer. Maybe [at the next race] in Monza we are, but I don't know.

"We're getting towards the end of the season, you also have to look at next year. I think there are a few things on the car we are looking at that can only be changed next year, to really find a lot more performance."

Red Bull did not bring a major upgrade to Zandvoort, only a new front corner, so team boss Laurent Mekies says they need to understand if their lack of performance was circuit specific, or to do with previous upgrades.

"Performance-wise I think there is nowhere to hide. It was a very difficult weekend. It seems we have made a bit of a step back compared to where we were before the summer break," he said.

"Of course we will never know what the real pace of the car would have been with Max. It's fair to say session after session it looked more difficult than it was in Budapest or Spa or Austria."

articles.title: Dutch GP: Mercedes boss Toto Wolff defends decision to order George Russell to let team-mate Kimi Antonelli past in Zandvoort race
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli extended his world championship lead after finishing second in the Dutch Grand Prix; George Russell was third after letting his Mercedes team-mate through in the closing stages following a team order; Mercedes boss Toto Wolff says the call was "not a difficult decision"
articles.body:
Championship leader Antonelli was running second to Lando Norris with 16 laps to go when Mercedes decided to pit the Italian for fresh tyres under a virtual safety car, bringing him out in third behind Russell.

It quickly became apparent that Antonelli didn't have the pace to challenge Norris for victory, but while he soon closed up on Russell, the difficulty of overtaking at Zandvoort meant there was no guarantee the Italian would be able to cruise past his team-mate.

However, Russell was told over the radio to allow Antonelli through into second, which would leave the Brit vulnerable to losing his place on the podium to Lewis Hamilton, on fresh tyres behind him with his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc in tow.

With the help of another VSC interruption, Russell did brilliantly to hold off Hamilton, but finishing behind Antonelli meant the gap between them at the top of the championship increased to 59 points.

Wolff told Sky Sports F1 : "We had a free stop with Kimi - a team internal free stop - and George was incredibly at the end fighting and also fending off the Ferraris, who were on a much quicker car. Was really, really exceptional.

"That (the decision) looks difficult on the outside but not on the inside. It's a situation we discussed very often, also today in the morning 'we're not going to lose time fighting with each other and have two Ferraris breathing down our neck'.

"So, it would have been the other way around exactly the same. It plays no role who is ahead in the championship or not, it's just about protecting the best possible positions."

Wolff insisted that his focus has to be on the best result for the team, rather than worrying about the feelings of his drivers.

"I don't think Antonelli was anywhere near catching Norris," Wolff added.

"It was just the safest way in terms of scoring points. You could have played maybe leaving him in the Overtake Mode and then again, you are risking too much, you have two Ferraris all over you.

"So, it was some tough calls, but they need to be done when you want to fight for the constructors' and drivers' championship.

"This is how we are operating. Both drivers know that. We avoid situations like some other teams where it's not clearly talked like this.

"This is harsh times, there's 2,500 people who work for championships, and it's not one man's game. That's how we operate it the last 15 years."

Russell initially appeared to question the order over the radio as he asked whether Antonelli had a chance of catching Norris, but ultimately quickly followed the instruction.

Asked about his thought process at the time, Russell said: "We've always said as a team, when we're on different strategies, we're never going to fight and we're always going to invert, and that's always just been our sort of rules.

"And the fact is Kimi was ahead of me before the VSC and he tried something different to protect us as a team. He kind of copy-pasted what the Ferraris did.

"Could I have kept him behind? Maybe. But equally, it could have been a P5 as well.

"So, in the end, he deserved to be P2. I think P3 was a fair result for me."

Antonelli: George made my life a lot easier

Antonelli thanked Russell for obeying the team order but admitted he felt as though his strategy had put his team-mate at greater risk of losing a podium.

The 19-year-old took the lead by passing Norris at an early restart but was unable to match the McLaren driver's impressive pace once they switched to the hard tyre compound at the first round of pit stops.

Antonelli said: "It was a difficult second half (of the race) for me, especially in the last stint on the hards, just really struggling. Had little confidence in the car and, yeah, it was not easy.

"And then obviously we pitted, and also that was a bit tricky. But then also George, I have to thank him because he made my life a lot easier.

"But I still think probably could have stayed out and gone until the end with the same set because it put us a little bit at risk. Also, I feel we put George at risk with having to let me by and everything.

"But I still think, at the end of the day, it was a great team execution with how things were, and I think today P2 was the maximum we could have done because the pace of the McLarens, especially in the second half, was just too strong."

articles.title: Dutch Grand Prix: Lando Norris and McLaren 'don't have car' to fight for title
articles.summary: Lando Norris says he and McLaren "don't have the car I need to fight for a championship", despite a second consecutive win of the season at the Dutch Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Lando Norris says he and McLaren "don't have the car I need to fight for a championship", despite a second consecutive win to open the second half of the Formula 1 season.

The Briton's victory in the final Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort, following on from his first win of the season in Hungary last month, was of the highest calibre.

As such, it raises the prospect of the sort of championship fightback staged by Red Bull's Max Verstappen against Norris himself last year.

After this race last year, Norris' team-mate Oscar Piastri had a 34-point advantage over the Briton and 104 over Verstappen. Yet Verstappen, after one of the all-time great fightbacks, finished the season just two points behind Norris as he won the title in Abu Dhabi.

Norris' masterful victory in Zandvoort has left him 83 points off the lead, held by Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli, who he and McLaren passed on track after losing the lead at the chaotic start of the day.

Antonelli's team-mate George Russell is tied on points with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, 59 behind the Italian.

Norris beats Antonelli to claim final Dutch GP win Published 2 days ago

Norris beats Antonelli to claim final Dutch GP win

Russell impresses as Norris shines - driver ratings Published 2 days ago

Russell impresses as Norris shines - driver ratings

Mercedes lack money to develop car like rivals - Wolff Published 2 days ago

Mercedes lack money to develop car like rivals - Wolff

But while McLaren have made a major step forward with upgrades to their car that led to convincing wins in both Hungary and now the Netherlands, Norris believes that the car still has too many flaws to mount the sort of consistent attack Verstappen produced last year.

"I'm confident because we clearly have a strong car," he said. "We have a strong car in certain areas. It's not like last year where we were pretty good everywhere.

"We're very, very strong in high speed, and that's the place we've improved the car the most, is high-speed performance. No one matches us in high speed, and that's a good thing.

"My pace advantage to Mercedes in Turn Seven, Eight was crazy, but their advantage that they have to us in slow speed is also crazy.

"And therefore, I don't have the confidence to say, 'Yeah, I can easily fight for a championship for the rest of the season.'

"I know I've just won two races in a row and had two poles in a row, but at the minute I don't have the car I need to fight for a championship. And I know that's quite a big comment."

Norris' belief is based on his understanding that McLaren's slow-speed performance will be a handicap at the next race in Monza, and two races after that in Azerbaijan.

Both tracks are dominated by long straights, which penalise the McLaren's high drag compared to Mercedes, and have very few high-speed corners where the car's strength can compensate for its weaknesses in slow turns.

McLaren team principal Andrea Stella said: âIf we can confirm our improvements in Monza, then we can look with some optimism at the remainder of the season.â

Norris' victory in Zandvoort, built around an off-set strategy and devastating pace once the cars were on the hard tyres in the second stint, underlined the level at which he is now operating.

As impressive as Verstappen's revival was last year, Norris' own in the second half of the season was almost as good, as both made up ground on Piastri.

And Norris believes he has built on the progress he made in his driving after a difficult start to 2025 to perform on an even higher plane in 2026.

"I was driving at a high level the second half of last year," he said. "It's tough to say, but I do think it's a trickier car to drive this year in some ways. And I think you can see that because the gaps between team-mates are often bigger this year, I would say, than it was last year.

"I do believe I'm able to understand situations better, to understand the car in a better way. It's still just horrible to drive, but I'm doing a better job at just understanding this, relaying this to my team, figuring stuff out.

"So, it's not just I'm driving better on track. I'm certainly eliminating my weaknesses on track, and I don't have so many, but it's also how I work off the track. And for me, yesterday to today is a perfect example of the work we put in overnight transformed our race and gave me the opportunity to win."

Team principal Andrea Stella said he believed Norris was driving better than ever.

"Lando is driving and operating at a very high level," Stella said. "He's driving at the level of a world champion.

"What I like the most of his journey in Formula 1 is that he keeps improving.

"After the start of the 2025 season, something clicked, which is not only a single click, but it's a way of working with Lando, for Lando, and that we are adopting also on Oscar's side now in particular.

"This approach has led Lando to continuous improvements.

"It's almost like I see Lando stronger and stronger race by race. Because I think this weekend was nowhere near a weekend in which we could fight for the victory for granted, especially after having seen the performance in the sprint (in which Norris was passed by Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and finished third).

"But we invested in trying to understand where was the opportunity from a tyre exploitation point of view and car improvement.

"And then when you have conditions in which the car slides in the race, there's not much grip, then I think he is the master in these kind of conditions."

A couple of months ago, before the British Grand Prix, and before McLaren had won a race this season, Norris admitted in an interview with BBC Sport "a little bit" of frustration at not being able to defend the title he won last year.

So it's perhaps no surprise that now he appears to have at least an outside chance of making a fist of it, he is not making any presumptions.

"One race at a time," he said. "I know a lot of people say it now, but it's the truth of it. There's no point thinking that far ahead.

"Obviously, two great weekends, but there's still plenty of things we can do better, and we need to do better if we want to fight for a championship.

"It's still harder than I would like, and I don't want a bigger gap, so we have to keep working hard. There's still plenty of races, plenty of opportunity for everyone. So, keep my head down, keep working, and they'll keep coming."

McLaren's progress has come in the context of stagnation at Mercedes, whose lack of an upgrade to their car since Canada in May has led to them being caught by McLaren and Ferrari, a situation that has raised eyebrows among rival teams.

The next Mercedes upgrade is not due until the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia in four races' time.

For Antonelli - who also faces a grid penalty at his home race in Italy next time out because he needs to take a new engine that exceeds his allowance as a consequence of early-season reliability problems - it cannot come soon enough.

"Now as a team we need to find a little bit of time because McLaren have done a huge step," he said.

"So for sure, in this race, it's going to be more difficult, it's going to be challenging, but we're ready to do our best and to maximise every opportunity.

"And then hopefully it's going to be our turn to bring the package that's going to give us a little bit of the upper hand again."

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver makes comparison to Mercedes' Dutch GP strategy call after radio frustrations
articles.summary: "It is difficult when you are looking ahead and you see the two Mercedes drivers, they get the call and it's done, and they execute straight away"; Hamilton expressed frustration over Ferrari team radio after being caught behind team-mate Charles Leclerc when lapping quickly on fresh tyres
articles.body:
Hamilton described his Sunday in Zandvoort as "definitely frustrating for me" after he was unable to find a way past Mercedes' George Russell for third place in the closing laps.

The seven-time world champion's irritation peaked on team radio midway through the race when he caught up with team-mate Charles Leclerc.

On fresher tyres after making a later pit stop than his team-mate, Hamilton initially pointed out as he arrived at the back of the sister Ferrari: "I'm quicker than Charles. These tyres are better."

However, Ferrari opted against reversing the order of the cars, which then led to an unusually-curt Hamilton barking: "We are just losing time!" Then, once Leclerc had pitted, Hamilton sarcastically returned to the radio to say: "A great way of wasting time guys, good job."

He went on to finish fourth on the tail of Russell, who had been instructed by Mercedes in the closing laps to let his team-mate Kimi Antonelli back by when the Italian caught the Briton on significantly faster and fresher tyres - decisive team tactics not lost on Hamilton.

Asked after the race about his blunt radio messages, Hamilton told F1 : "I want to win. I want to win. I'm here to win.

"It is difficult when you are looking ahead and you see the two Mercedes drivers, they get the call and it's done, and they execute straight away.

"They let Kimi by and let him get on with the race. I was on a different strategy and it's not the same here.

"That's a little bit difficult but we'll take it offline and when I go back now, I'll speak to them about it."

'My goal is to try and lead this team to the championship'

Although Ferrari were outqualified by McLaren and Mercedes for both the sprint and main grand prix at Zandvoort, their longer-run pace was more impressive and they again became a factor in the podium hunt.

Hamilton, who had started fifth, praised the latest round of upgrades brought to the SF-26 for the first race after the summer break but expressed regret they had not been able to get a little more out of Sunday.

He told Sky Sports F1 : "Firstly, the guys in the garage did a fantastic job. Pit stops, strategy was generally very, very good. The car felt awesome and they have continued to work so hard.

"We brought a bit of an upgrade here. We are just chipping away at it all the time. This first half of the season we have been losing three to five tenths on the straight depending on which track we go to and that's a hard deficit to overcome just through the corners. But we are close.

"But today was definitely frustrating for me.

"I'm here to win and I really believe that this team can win.

"We couldn't win this race but to win championships you have to pick up every point and the last few races have been difficult with penalties and stuff and then, today, I lost several seconds behind Charles which I think ultimately would have made the difference at the end.

"But we will take it offline. My goal is to try and lead this team to the championship and we've got some work to do for sure."

Finishing behind title leader Antonelli for the second day running, Hamilton left Zandvoort an increased 59 points off the Mercedes driver in the championship.

articles.title: Melania Trump talks about foster care initiative, racing interest at Freedom 250 Grand Prix
articles.summary: First lady Melania Trump on Sunday shared how her father got her into racing during an interview at the Freedom 250 Grand Prix event. “Yes, when I was growing up, my father introduced me to the races and to the race cars, and he owned some incredible cars from Maserati and Cougar and Mustang, Mercedes,”…
articles.body:
First lady Melania Trump on Sunday shared how her father got her into racing during an interview at the Freedom 250 Grand Prix event.

“Yes, when I was growing up, my father introduced me to the races and to the race cars, and he owned some incredible cars from Maserati and Cougar and Mustang, Mercedes,” Trump told Fox Sports on Sunday.

“So, he introduced me to design of the cars and the mechanics, and also the speed, and I loved it, every minute of it,” she added.

Fox Sports’s Jamie Little then transitioned the conversation to talk about Fostering the Future, a scholarship program for foster care students which has been Trump’s main focus during her second term as first lady.

“They need to have the same opportunity as other children,” Trump said when asked about the initiative’s importance, calling its accomplishments “incredible.”

The first lady on Thursday announced a partnership with IndyCar and Fox Corporation, with the two companies donating a combined $2 million to fund additional scholarships.

In March, IndyCar unveiled that it would host the first street race on the National Mall in August, the Freedom 250 Grand Prix. The course, which is 1.7 miles, loops around the National Archives, National Gallery of Art and Smithsonian Air and Space Museum.

President Trump’s motorcade took him on a lap around the event’s racetrack Sunday. The race is part of semiquincentennial celebrations, featuring flyovers from multiple military branches .

The president announced the race via executive order earlier this year, with the event having a goal of showing off “the majesty of our great city as drivers navigate a track around our iconic national monuments in celebration of America’s 250th birthday.”

articles.summary: Primera sesión oficial de monoplazas en el nuevo trazado de Ifema, con una de las categorías que competirá del 11 al 13 de septiembre junto a la F1
articles.body: A solo 19 días del primer Gran Premio de España en Madring, el circuito madrileño recibe hoy su bautismo competitivo oficial. Se trata del test de F3, con presencia de Bruno del Pino (sobrino de Pedro de la Rosa), como representante español y que tomará el primer sabor verdadero de una pista ya terminada y preparada para la competición de monoplazas.  En la pista estarán todos los monoplazas de la categoría, que este fin de semana no han corrido en Zandvoort y que regresan a la actividad para encarar la parte final de la temporada 2026. Es una buena ocasión para ver cómo se desarrollan las pruebas en en Madring y cómo se ubican 31 monoplazas en esta pista y por sus distintas zonas, como ensayo general para dentro de tres semanas, en una pista mucho más rápida de lo que se pensaba inicialmente. Los coches empezaron a rodar a las 9.00 de la mañana y los pilotos se tomaron su tiempo para reconocer la pista, con vueltas de instalación sin tiempos por el momento. El 'pit building', o el nuevo edificio que alberga los boxes y parte del Paddock Club de la F1, está terminado por completo, después de varios meses de montaje, que comenzó en el mes de enero.  En lo deportivo, Del Pino se colocaba primero sobre las 10.10 de la mañana, cuando tras una hora de actividad casi todos los equipos empezaban a apretar. Su tiempo era de 1:52.6, rebajando casi en cada intento por la mañana, cuando el crono estimado para la vuelta de F1 está sobre 1:34.4. Al final de la mañana, Del Pino tuvo un pequeño toque con el muro, dañando una llanta y la suspensión delantera de su coche, pero sin consecuencias graves. El de Barcelona era segundo en la tabla, superado por Ugochukwu (Campos Racing). Los tiempos eran de 1;51 en ese momen to, aunque en el simulador los pilotos ya estaban haciendo esta semana 1:46, por lo que la pista tiene mucho margen de mejora. Una hora se perdió el español de la sesión vespertina, hasta que le fue reparado el coche. Muy rápido volvía a estar en tiempos competitivos.  Al final del día, fue Slater el mejor del día, con 1:50.2, a pesar del viento racheado que se levanto en las dos últimas horas. Se quedaban a unos tres segundos de los tiempos de simulador, aunque en la jornada del martes bajarán los cronos de nuevo.

articles.summary: La votación de los aficionados de todo el mundo a la F1 se lo dieron a Norris por escaso margen
articles.body: Fernando Alonso, con un noveno puesto y con una estrategia a una parada menos, se quedó a un paso de lograr el título de piloto del día en la carrera de Holanda este domingo. El asturiano no deja de tener un tirón especial entre los aficionados a la F1 de todo el mundo, lo que le ha valido un reconocimiento especial en cuanto ha vuelto a tener un coche para luchar por objetivos. Cuando vayan llegando los nuevos pasos en el chasis, que en Monza podría estar ya en los 768 kg de peso mínimo que marca el reglamento 2026 y cuando Honda vaya puliendo la manejabilidad de su nuevo motor, el asturiano podrá meterse en luchas mayores, seguramente para la carrera de Madring, donde el equilibrio entre motor y chasis será más favorable que en Italia. El caso es que con una buena primera vuelta, donde ganó tres plazas, carrera en cuanto a ritmo, Fernando estuvo valorado casi a la par de Norris, que acabó la prueba de forma estelar, pasando a Antonelli y Hamilton para llevarse su segunda victoria de la temporada (tras la cosechada en Hungría).  Es la demostración de que Lando no es uno de los más carismáticos de la parrilla actual, donde Verstappen y Alonso siguen ofreciendo ese plus de magnetismo que no todos los deportistas tienen.  Además, Fernando superó a un Hamilton (13%) que estuvo liderando hasta la parte final de la prueba y vendió caro el segundo luego frente a Antonelli.

articles.title: Mercedes, +59 de Antonelli y excusas: “No tenemos el dinero de nuestros rivales”
articles.standfirst: Desde el equipo de la estrella consideran que sus rivales les han ganado la carrera de las novedades por una razón clara: el dinero
articles.summary: Desde el equipo de la estrella consideran que sus rivales les han ganado la carrera de las novedades por una razón clara: el dinero
articles.body: Andrea Kimi Antonelli sigue quemando etapas a una velocidad bárbara pese a no tener esa pólvora de inicio de temporada cuando encadenó varios triunfos al hilo que dispararon su candidatura al título mundial. Vivió malos momentos en Barcelona o Silverstone (ceros por motivos ajenos ), pero se repone con una solidez inesperada. Ya llegó al parón fuerte tras un carrerón en Hungría y lo refrendó con un segundo de oro en el Gran Premio de los Países Bajos. Su balance es aterrador, con 59 puntos al frente de la Fórmula 1. Con esos argumentos y un coche superior en buena parte de los circuitos del calendario, el italiano apunta a ser el grandísimo favorito. Pero Mercedes, que siempre juega en el hilar fino de las verdades con asteriscos y vueltas de tuerca, no lo ve tan claro. Si bien es cierto que su coche se cayó en la segunda parte de Zandvoort (en la rueda dura), los de la estrella ven que es un asunto clave en comparación con el resto. Y tienen su motivo claro: “No tenemos el dinero del resto de rivales para mejorar”. La frase, por supuesto, viene de su máximo representante, Toto Wolff. El dirigente de Austria se ha encontrado con una McLaren al alza, Ferrari con batería de novedades en el arsenal de Maranello y sólo claramente por delante de Red Bull. Le preocupa de cara a defender los intereses de Antonelli y Russell, 1° y 2° en la tabla. “No tenemos el dinero, intentamos trabajar con ello esta temporada y debemos repartirlas de forma equitativa basándonos en cuando pueden ser más óptimas para obtener puntos”, analizaba. Ese dinero es el techo presupuestario de los equipos, cifrado en unos 215 millones de dólares para cada equipo. “Es lo que podemos hacer. Es una carrera de desarrollo y si tienes una mejora, cada equipo puntero ganará unas pocas décimas y es lo que pierdes”, explicó Wolff. Su coche, de cualquier forma, sigue dominando con mano de hierro y el milagro de Norris debería venir desde los 83 puntos de desventaja. Hamilton, con Ferrari, está a 59 (como Russell) pero el SF-26 no es superior al Mercedes. Entre las estrellas de la F1, el mensaje de Mercedes tiene respaldo en sus pilotos, aunque Norris, señalado por la fuerza de su McLaren, es más cauto. “No creo que quieran decir que ellos mismos son los más rápidos. No creo que quieran decir que son el equipo a batir. Pero sí han sido batidos, y es la realidad. Pero si no pasaba a Kimi, no hubiese ganado la carrera”, relató Norris. Los capítulos de la película seguirán y todavía en Monza se espera algo más tras la segura sanción de Antonelli al montar un nuevo motor. Con Wolff calmando las aguas tras ver su mando con fuertes opositores en el resto de contendientes. “Sí, está siendo más difícil que en el inicio de año”, cerró.
